summary: The Madagascar trip the audience voted for, and the channel opens the thread by calling everyone who voted for it to gather. The most affecting comment is from someone who says she has few friends and rarely leaves the house, and watching this feels like living out the dream by proxy — she asks them never to stop. Destination requests continue, with India and Japan argued for on the grounds of what would happen to this specific group there. Viewers notice small acts of inclusion, singling out the moment a host turned the camera to bring a crew member into frame. There is also role recognition: Natty is identified as the one holding the trip together while everyone else falls apart.

audience_signals: Closing the loop on the vote — calling the voters back to the episode they chose — turns a one-off poll into a returning-audience mechanic
A meaningful part of this audience is socially isolated and watches for substitute companionship, which explains why friendship beats destination in every comment thread
Viewers assign roles to cast members (the stabiliser, the chaos, the comic) and track them across episodes; the group works as an ensemble cast
Destination requests come with reasoning about what would happen to this group there, so viewers are pitching scenarios rather than places
content_requests: Take the group to India and to Japan
